<description>
As discussed in #36403, one of the issues with current rebroadcast behavior is that the rebroadcast begins an unconditional relay of a transaction to peers. While this is broadcast is limited to peers that have not previously been inv'd the transaction, there is still a privacy leak in this double relay of a transaction, especially so for transactions that are still in nodes' mempools.

This PR changes the rebroadcast to only rebroadcast transactions if the transaction was not already present in our mempool. This provides some additional privacy while retaining intended rebroadcast behavior as transactions that have likely fallen out of nodes' mempools are the ones that actually need to be rebroadcast.

The wallet rebroadcast tests are additionally refactored for isolation so that their behaviors can still be tested after this change. Additionally, a test for the loading resubmission was added, as well as a test for the new behavior.
</description>

[2026-10-21] r:5604335981 review COMMENTED by murchandamus (member):
This PR introduces the new `MEMPOOL_AND_BROADCAST_ADDED` TxBroadcast case, and uses it when the wallet resubmits transactions to the node’s mempool instead of the transaction being rebroadcast to all peers that it hadn’t been inventoried. The tests check that the rebroadcast happens when the transaction is added to the mempool and doesn’t happen when the transaction was already present. This is an obvious privacy improvement.

The only open question I have at the moment is whether the combination of using `MEMPOOL_NO_BROADCAST` on wallet loading and then `MEMPOOL_AND_BROADCAST_ADDED` on the wallet’s rebroadcast could prevent a transaction from being resubmitted to the network. E.g., if a wallet submits a low-feerate transaction, then the node is turned off for some period during which a feerate spike causes most of the network to drop the transaction, then the node is turned back on, wouldn’t this mean that the wallet’s transaction is not rebroadcast at all?

Also, I’m not sure whether using `MEMPOOL_AND_BROADCAST_ADDED` during wallet loading would fix that, if the node still had the transaction in its mempool from before going offline.
</new_statements>
